text:
Maya Chen: hey team! i’m Maya (frontend eng, started today) — trying to get my dev env up on an M1 MacBook Air. running into asdf/python/node quirks. anyone around?
David R: welcome Maya! share the specific errors you see. most folks hit openssl / brew path stuff on Apple Silicon.
Maya Chen: thanks! when i run `ruby -v` in a repo it says wrong openssl or gem native extension fails. i installed asdf via brew and added to zshrc per the quickstart.
Olga Petrov: did you add the asdf shims to your PATH and run `asdf reshim` after plugins? also check `brew --prefix openssl@1.1` path for LDFLAGS/CFLAGS.
Maya Chen: i did `echo $PATH` and see `~/.asdf/shims` earlier than brew, and `~/.zshrc` has the asdf init lines. sample error: 
```
Building native extensions.
current directory: /Users/maya/.asdf/installs/ruby/2.7.6/gems/pg-1.2.3/ext
checking for pg_config... no\n*** extconf.rb failed ***
```
Maya Chen: looks like pg_config from postgres not found.
Samir Patel: on mac arm, i usually `brew install libpq` then `brew link --force libpq` or set `PATH="$(brew --prefix libpq)/bin:$PATH"` before installing the gem. for openssl you may need: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib" CFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"`
David R: +1. Also for ruby via asdf, run `RUBY_CONFIGURE_OPTS=--with-openssl-dir=$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1) asdf install ruby 2.7.6` so it builds against homebrew openssl.
Maya Chen: ah ok will try that. any dotfiles / zshrc examples people recommend? mine is basically from dotfiles repo but i get warnings about `source ~/.aliases` failing on new shell.
Olga Petrov: make sure dotfiles submodules are cloned. we have a tiny onboarding repo with recommended ~/.zshrc for macs. @dev-onboard-bot should have posted a link when you signed up.
dev-onboard-bot: Hi Maya! welcome 🎉 — onboarding checklist: https://intranet.redwood/handbook/onboarding/dev-setup — includes asdf + brew snippets and our recommended dotfiles.
Maya Chen: got the checklist, thanks bot :) i still have one thing: node versions. `asdf nodejs` seems to require gpg keys import and `corepack` conflicts. i get EACCES when npm tries to create global folders.
Samir Patel: for node, use `asdf plugin-add nodejs` then `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` (gpg). then `asdf install nodejs 16.20.0` etc. for npm perms, avoid `sudo` — either change npm global prefix or just use project-local `npx`/pnpm/yarn. we prefer pnpm: `npm i -g pnpm` then `pnpm i` inside projects.
Maya Chen: great. last one: env vars. rails dev needs `DATABASE_URL` and `REDWOOD_API_KEY_DEV`. where do new hires get keys?
David R: file a request in #help with "new-hire dev keys" and tag @Olga. we auto-provision local dev keys that expire in 90 days. For secrets in dotfiles, we recommend using `~/.local/envrc` (ignored by git) and `direnv` — we have a template in the onboarding repo.
Maya Chen: direnv makes sense. i’ll add `export DATABASE_URL=postgres://mayanet:pass@localhost:5432/devdb` to `~/.local/envrc` and `echo 'use dotenv' > .envrc` ?
Olga Petrov: we use `direnv allow` on the project root and store `.envrc.example` in repos. don't commit creds.
Samir Patel: if you run into weird asdf shim ordering, verify `~/.zshrc` has these lines in this order:
```
# asdf setup
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
. ~/.asdf/completions/asdf.bash
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
```
Maya Chen: awesome — i'm going to try these commands now. thanks all!
David R: ping here if you still hit issues, or drop into #eng-devex for pairing. also happy to do a quick screenshare later. :)
Maya Chen: quick update — `RUBY_CONFIGURE_OPTS=--with-openssl-dir=$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1) asdf install ruby 2.7.6` worked, pg gem installed after `brew install libpq` and `export PATH="$(brew --prefix libpq)/bin:$PATH"`. node import key step needed gpg but fixed. dotfiles issue was missing git submodule. all green now 👍
Olga Petrov: yay! welcome aboard — we have a team lunch tomorrow, i'll DM details.
Samir Patel: added you to pnpm/npm group in our internal permissions so you won't need global installs.
Maya Chen: thanks everyone, closing the thread :)
